Cc: integrations@logstream.io, security@clearmind.com

Subject: Audit event mapping & sprint asks — operator-level logs / BYOK overlap

Team — starting a short thread to align product asks and what we need to deliver for ClearMind's audit evidence request (see attached). Key ask from the customer: a filterable export of operator-level events (keystore ops, BYOK handoffs, SSO session binds) with 30d retention and metadata for end-to-end linkage to their own SIEM.

Quick goals for this thread:
- Confirm which events we can provide from hosted vs. Dedicated/Private.
- Clarify whether we can include KMS key IDs and ephemeral key TTLs in exported rows or need redaction.
- Identify the earliest sprint we can surface a CSV/JSON export and a query interface for their security team.

I've attached a first-pass audit-event-mapping spreadsheet — column headers are proposals not final. Please review and reply with redlines. I want a consolidated response to ClearMind by EOD Friday so we don't block procurement.

— Markus

----

From: ClearMind Health <security@clearmind.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-13T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Audit event mapping & sprint asks — operator-level logs / BYOK overlap

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the spreadsheet. A couple clarifications from our side:
1) We need a persistent identifier we can join to our SSO logs — ideally a session_id or traced request_id. IPs are fragile for our environment.
2) When you say "operator-level" we mean any action that affects customer key material or key access policies (rotate, escrow, handback). We need timestamps, actor identity, key-id, and success/failure.
3) For KMS-related events, does Redwood store any plaintext key material in logs? If so we need confirmation of redaction practices.

Can you confirm if the export can be scoped to specific projects/tenant ids and whether we can schedule daily exports to our S3 bucket?

— L. Park (ClearMind SecOps)

----

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, integrations@logstream.io, security@clearmind.com
Date: 2026-12-14T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Audit event mapping & sprint asks — operator-level logs / BYOK overlap

Thanks Liz + Markus. Quick product perspective:
- Hosted API: we currently emit structured audit events for model inference and route decisions; however operator-level KMS handoffs for BYOK are stored in an internal keystore service and the emitted audit record today is minimal (action, timestamp, customer_id). We do NOT log plaintext key material.
- Dedicated/Private: customers who run Redwood Private often have the ability to keep full keystore telemetry locally; for hosted we need to determine acceptable metadata surface (key-id vs hashed key-pointer).

Concrete asks for engineering/infra backlog: 
1) Add fields to audit events: session_id (string), operation_subtype (rotate|handback|import|export), key_pointer_hash (sha256), key_rotation_result (success/failure), operator_principal (email or service id), request_id (trace).
2) Export path: S3 push + API query endpoint with tenant filter and delivery schedule (daily/weekly).
3) Retention controls per tenant — default 30d but allow enterprise 365d via plan.

Timeline proposition: small schema change + export worker — feasible in a 3-week sprint if we scope to CSV daily exports. For an interactive query UI we should target next quarter.

I'll attach a trimmed mapping for infra to review.

— Priyom

----

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, integrations@logstream.io
Date: 2026-12-15T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Audit event mapping & sprint asks — operator-level logs / BYOK overlap

All — product notes and constraints:
- We can ship the CSV export for hosted customers, but KMS metadata must be non-sensitive by default. Proposal: expose key_id (opaque UUID) + key_pointer_hash; do NOT include customer-provided KEK material.
- Session_id: we already surface a request_id for inference traces; extending that to session-level SSO correlation will require a lightweight handshake in the auth flow (adds ~1 sprint of work to Auth infra).
- Retention toggle: product can offer a plan-level opt-in for >30d; legal sign-off needed for 365d default.

Questions for Security: can we use a deterministic hashed key pointer (sha256 of key-id + tenant salt) for joinability without leaking raw key ids? Is that acceptable for audit evidence?

Marissa

----

From: LogStream Integrations <integrations@logstream.io>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: security@clearmind.com, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-16T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Audit event mapping & sprint asks — operator-level logs / BYOK overlap

Hi all — quick technical caveat from the vendor side.
- Our S3 ingestion expects structured JSON with stable column names. The key_pointer_hash approach works as long as the salt is consistent for the tenant across exports. If Redwood rotates the salt, joins will break.
- We recommend adding a "join_hint" field which can be a stable, non-reversible encoding (e.g., HMAC with tenant-scoped secret) that we can use to join with SSO session ids.
- Note on delivery: signed URL push from Redwood to our ingestion role is simplest. Doc attached with our preferred schema.

— LogStream integrations team

Attachments to send to ClearMind on sign-off: audit-event-mapping-v1.xlsx, clearmind-evidence-ask-20261212.pdf.
